intro.title: Test Context
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll learn how to use Test Context in Vue to write clean and maintainable tests. You'll build a simple counter component and create tests that verify its behavior works correctly. The core concept is understanding how to set up a testing environment with proper component mounting and data isolation. You'll work with Vue Test Utils and Jest to create test suites that validate your component's functionality. This will help you write reliable tests that don't interfere with each other.
intro.usecase: Test Context is a fundamental pattern in Vue for managing and sharing state or logic across multiple components in a unit test suite. In real-world applications, developers use test contexts to isolate and control the environment for testing complex UI features like interactive dashboards, multi-step forms, or dynamic data tables. For example, when testing a dashboard that fetches live data, a test context can mock API responses and provide consistent state, ensuring each component test runs independently and reliably. This pattern is essential for maintaining scalable, maintainable test suites in large-scale Vue applications, such as e-commerce platforms or admin panels, where components depend on shared services or global state.
